==English==
{{wp}}
[[Image:Palanca-ejemplo.jpg|thumb|A lever]]
[[Image:LeverPrincleple.svg|thumb|A lever diagram]]

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈliː.və/|a=RP|ref={{R:Lexico}}<<name:ODO>>}}
*: {{audio|en|en-uk-lever.ogg|a=Gloucestershire}}
*: {{hyphenation|en|le|ver}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛv.ɚ/|/ˈli.vɚ/|a=GA,CA}},<ref name="MWO">{{R:MWO}}</ref><ref name="AHD">{{R:AHD}}</ref>
*: {{audio|en|II US lever.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈliː.və/|a=AU}}
*: {{hyphenation|en|lev|er||le|ver}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːvə(ɹ)|ɛvə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{homophones|en|leaver|Lever}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁lengʷʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|lever}}, {{m|enm|levore}}, {{m|enm|levour}}, from {{der|en|fro|leveor}}, {{m|fro|leveur|t=a lifter, lever (also {{der|en|fro|-}} and {{der|en|fr|levier}})}}, from {{der|en|la|levātor|t=a lifter}}, from {{m|la|levō|t=to raise}}. {{doublet|en|levator}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|mechanics}} A [[rigid]] piece which is capable of [[turn]]ing about one point, or [[axis]] ([[fulcrum]]), and in which are two or more other points where forces are applied; — used for transmitting and modifying force and motion.
## Specifically, a [[bar]] of metal, wood or other rigid substance, used to exert a pressure, or sustain a weight, at one point of its length, by receiving a force or power at a second, and turning at a third on a fixed point called a fulcrum. It is usually named as the first of the six mechanical powers, and is of three kinds, according as either the fulcrum F, the weight W, or the power P, respectively, is situated between the other two, as in the figures.
# A small such piece to [[trigger]] or [[control]] a mechanical device (like a [[switch]] or a [[button]]).
# {{lb|en|mechanics}} A [[bar]], as a [[capstan bar]], applied to a rotatory piece to turn it.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03
|author=w:Henry Petroski
|title=Opening Doors
|volume=100|issue=2|page=112–3
|magazine=w:American Scientist
|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/opening-doors
|passage=A doorknob of whatever roundish shape is effectively a continuum of '''levers''', with the axis of the latching mechanism—known as the spindle—being the fulcrum about which the turning takes place.}}
# {{lb|en|mechanics}} An [[arm]] on a [[rock shaft]], to give motion to the shaft or to obtain motion from it.
# {{lb|en|obsolete|except in generalized senses below}} A [[crowbar]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1613|author=w:John Marston; William Barksted|title=The Insatiate Countess|section=IV.1
|passage=My lord, I brained him with a '''lever''' my neighbour lent me, and he stood by and cried, ‘Strike home, old boy!’}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[move]] with a [[lever#Noun|lever]].
#: {{syn|en|purchase}}
#: {{ux|en|With great effort and a big crowbar I managed to '''lever''' the beam off the floor.}}
#* {{RQ:Orwell Homage|chapter=7|passage=Someone found a pick and '''levered''' a burst plank out of the floor, and in a few minutes we had got a fire alight and our drenched clothes were steaming.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|transitive}} To [[use]], [[operate]] or [[move]] (something) like a [[lever#Noun|lever]] (physically).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1950|author=Norman Lindsay|authorlink=Norman Lindsay|title={{w|Dust or Polish?}}|publisher=Angus and Robertson|location=Sydney|page=150|passage=Sullen now, with stultified spleen, Mrs Dibble grappled her crutches and '''levered''' herself upright after an ungainly struggle.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author=w:V. S. Naipaul|title=w:A House for Mr Biswas|publisher=Vintage International|year_published=2001|section=Part Two, Chapter 1
|passage=Suddenly he had '''levered''' himself up from the sofa, rocking the lame man violently, and was walking towards the receptionist.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|transitive}} To [[use]] (something) like a [[lever#Noun|lever]] (in an abstract sense).
#* {{RQ:Time|author=w:Joshua Cooper Ramo|title=Bagging the Butcher|date=9 April 2001|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130823124907/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,999627,00.html
|passage=He was a man who '''levered''' his way from small-time communist hack to political power by tapping into the most potent vein of historical juice in the Balkans: nationalism.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=w:Robert McCrum|title=Biographies of the year — review|date=8 December 2013|url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2013/dec/08/biographies-of-the-year-2013-review
|passage=Credited with pioneering the detective novel, Collins has attracted many biographers over the years, drawn to his extraordinary life and work in the hope of '''levering''' open a new understanding of the Victorian psyche.}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly|_|UK|finance}} To [[increase]] the [[share]] of [[debt]] in the [[capitalization]] of a business.

===Etymology 2===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|id=love}}
From {{inh|en|enm|lever}}, comparative of {{m|en|leve}}, {{m|enm|leef|t=dear, beloved, lief}}, equivalent to {{af|en|lief|-er}}. Related to {{cog|de|lieber|t=rather}}.

====Alternative forms====

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[rather|Rather]].
#* {{RQ:Tyndale Jonah|chapter=4|verse=3|page=23|passage=Now therfore take my life from me / for I had '''leuer''' dye then liue.}}
#* {{RQ:John Heywood Four PP|sig=[E.ii.]|verso=1|page=81|passage=The wolde ſome mayſter perhappes clowt ye / But as for me ye nede nat doute ye / For I had '''leuer''' be without ye / Then haue ſuche beſyneſſe aboute ye.}}
#* {{RQ:Calvin Golding Psalmes|To the Readers|page=23|passage=For although they were worthy of any puniſhment: yit had I '''leuer''' they might haue flooriſhed in welfare and ſafetie: {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|I|IX|128|For '''leuer''' had I die, then ſee his deadly face.}}
